title: Rabbi Gamliel (V)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: His father, Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the second, was Rabbi Yochanan’s student; although he did not reach his fathers’ level, he was a great man. But his son Rabbi Gamliel did not reach his father’s level, by the testimony of Rabbi Abbahu in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:1: “Rabbi Abbahu said: And did not Rabban Gamliel Berabbi ask me whether it is permitted to go to a fair, and I forbade it to him? … How is that? Rabban Gamliel was a man of lesser standing, and Rabbi Abbahu wished to restrain him.” This Rabban Gamliel is likewise mentioned in Shabbat, chapter 6, end of halakhah 1: once he went down to stroll in his courtyard on Shabbat with a golden key in his hand, and his colleagues rebuked him.

In Hyman’s historical account, until his days the Patriarchs were in Tzippori and Tiberias, but in his days the sect of the Christians grew strong in the Land of Israel and destroyed several towns of Israel; therefore Rabbi Abbahu, who was close to and beloved by the government, took him under his wings to Caesarea. This is why we find him with Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Yochanan’s student. He suggests that possibly what we find in Ketubot 24b — “The Patriarch’s house seized an orphan’s maidservant; Rabbi Abbahu sat … Rabbi Abba said to him: Because of the Patriarch’s house you flatter him?” — is this Rabban Gamliel.

He is likewise mentioned in Midrash Tehillim 100:9: an incident in which Rabban Gamliel went to Rabbi Chelbo of Karuyah (the old Midrash Tehillim reads: to Abba Chalfa bar Kuriyah) and said to him, “Pray for me”; he said to him, “May He grant you according to your heart.” Abba Chalfa lived in the generation of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, which is the generation of this Rabban Gamliel. Hyman considers it very likely that the unnamed Patriarch in Moed Katan 22b — “The Patriarch died; Rav Chisda said to Rav Chanan bar Rabbah: Turn over the mortar and stand on it and show the rending to the world” — is this Rabban Gamliel. He explains in the entry Rav Chanan bar Rava that, because he was a native of the Land of Israel, Rav Chisda told him that he must show mourning over the Patriarch’s death. Since he was a man of lesser standing, his name is not mentioned. Hyman infers from this the time of his death, for it is known that Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the second died after Rav Yehudah, as explained in his entry; and this Rabban Gamliel died before Rav Chisda, who died in the year 620 of the Seleucid era (lishtarot). In his place sat Rabbi Yehudah Nesia the third, the father of Hillel, who established the calculation of intercalation.
